analysis.title: GS US TMT .. quick hits .. (Peter Callahan, 2 Nov 2026)
key_insights: NDX fell about 275 bps intraday to its 200-day moving average, led by semis. The SOX fell about 540 bps intraday and registered a new low close for the second half of the year, below the late-July lows.

NDX is down about 611 bps over the last 3 sessions, the biggest 3-day slide since Liberation Day roughly 20 months ago. The equal-weight S&P (RSP) is up about 1% over the same stretch, and the Russell 2000 is now outperforming the NDX on the year.

Desk flows show little defense across Semis/AI. Risk appetite is challenged in a 'wait and see' mode as catalysts have failed to restart AI/Semis momentum, and the market is more discerning on the linearity of the AI build-out beyond CY27, which is pressuring multiples.
Oil/crude fell and yields reached about 2-month lows, but the relief showed up only in consumer-facing tech (OTAs, Internet, Payments). AI/Tech closed on the lows of the day.
Top client inbounds: continued drag in INTC and AMD, why semis are so heavy, AMZN bounce sustainability, MRVL and LITE action, strength in analog semis, and why DDOG, RBRK, MDB and FTNT fell so much.
Most asked-about earnings this week: AAPL, PLTR, AMD, ANET, BKNG, DDOG, UBER, APP, EXPE, Unity, FWONK, MCHP, LYV, NET, ABNB.

GS Econ/GIR election preview expects the data center focus to fade after the election. Congress might limit data center tax incentives, a national moratorium looks unlikely, and the focus likely shifts to AI regulation, where restrictive regulation looks unlikely.

ISM manufacturing rose in October above expectations, with higher new orders and production, lower employment, and prices paid easing slightly. The Goldman Sachs Analyst Index fell 6.5pt to 49.1, below 50 for the first time since April 2025.
AAPL F4Q (reported after the close) beat on total revenue, iPhone revenue, gross margin and EPS. Services revenue was in line with consensus. The stock was +30 bps after hours, having been -2%.
Fabrinet (FN) rose 13% after hours on a beat and a guide above consensus for 2Q revenue and EPS.
PLTR rose 1% after hours on a headline beat and raise. US Commercial revenue grew 148% y/y, the FY US commercial growth guide was raised to above 143%, and the FY FCF guide was raised.

ON fell 2% after hours (off the lows). F3Q results were solid, F4Q revenue guide midpoint was below consensus, EPS guide was in line, and 3Q AI data center revenue grew 39% q/q and 175% y/y. ON is acquiring Ferric for about $600mn.

SBAC first take from GIR: site leasing revenue and tower cash flow missed, EBITDA was largely in line, 2026E guidance was lowered on forex and the Chile and Ecuador asset sale, AFFO rose slightly on lower maintenance capex, and the underlying outlook was unchanged.
Chart of the day: the S&P 500 low vol index has been negatively correlated to the Nasdaq since the summer, in the context of 30+ years of data.

market_movers.rationale: F4Q total revenue $114.5bn (+12% y/y) vs consensus $113.47bn, iPhone revenue $57.583bn vs $56.49bn, EPS $2.10 vs consensus about $2.00. Shares +30 bps after hours. Desk calls the print 'solid' and says the debate is about the multiple.
2Q revenue guide $1.6-1.65B vs consensus $1.48B and EPS guide $4.77-4.92 vs consensus $4.43. Shares +13% after hours.
Headline beat and raise. FY FCF guide raised to $4.8-5bn from $4.5-4.7bn and FY US commercial revenue growth guide raised to above 143% y/y. Shares +1% after hours.
F4Q revenue guide $1.715-1.815bn vs consensus $1.74bn and EPS guide 95c-$1.07 vs consensus 96c. Shares -2% after hours, off the lows.
GIR expects mixed trading on a site leasing revenue and tower cash flow miss, with 2026E guidance lowered on forex and asset sales.

sector_views.rationale: Desk flows show little defense in Semis/AI. The SOX made a new 2H low close and multiples are pressured by doubts about AI build-out linearity beyond CY27.
OTAs, Internet and Payments were the only tech pockets to gain from lower oil and yields while AI/Tech closed on the lows.

earnings_insights: AAPL F4Q reported 11/2 after the close: total revenue $114.5bn (+12% y/y) reported vs consensus $113.47bn (+10.7% y/y). Services revenue $31.573bn reported vs consensus $31.577bn. iPhone revenue $57.583bn reported vs consensus $56.49bn. Gross margin 47.9% reported (includes about 1pt tariff refund tailwind) vs consensus 47.6%. EPS $2.10 reported (includes 5c tariff tailwind) vs consensus about $2.00.

AAPL call at 5pm ET: focus on Duo and new products, gross margin outlook into C4Q, and C4Q revenue guide vs consensus of +6% y/y. Operating cash flow was $28 billion and $28 billion was returned to shareholders.
FN F2Q guide (given 11/2): revenue $1.6-1.65B vs consensus $1.48B and EPS $4.77-4.92 vs consensus $4.43.

PLTR 3Q reported 11/2: US total revenue +119% y/y (vs +115% last quarter), US Commercial revenue +148% y/y (vs +149%), US Commercial RDV $6.517bn (+4% q/q) vs $6.238bn last quarter, Rule of 40 at 158% (vs 155%). FY US commercial revenue growth guide raised to above 143% y/y from above 134%. FY FCF guide $4.8-5bn vs prior $4.5-4.7bn.

ON F3Q reported 11/2: revenue $1.722bn (+7.4% q/q) vs guide $1.70bn midpoint, gross margin 41.2% vs guide 40-42%, EPS 90c vs guide 81-93c, inventories $2,069mn. F4Q guide: revenue $1.715-1.815bn (+2.5% q/q at midpoint) vs consensus $1.74bn, gross margin 41.5-43.5%, EPS 95c-$1.07 vs consensus 96c. 3Q AI data center revenue +39% q/q and +175% y/y.

SBAC 3Q reported 11/2: site leasing revenue and tower cash flow missed consensus, EBITDA largely in line. 2026E guidance lowered on tower cash flow and EBITDA due to forex and the Chile and Ecuador asset sale (closed 9/10). AFFO increased slightly on lower maintenance capex (GIR first take).

Earnings after the close 11/2: AAPL, AEIS, FN, MTCH, ON, PLTR, ROKU, SBAC, UPWK, VOYG, WAY. Earnings 11/3 pre-market: CLVT, DOCN, DT, ETN, FISV, IPGP, LBTYA, SHOP, TeamViewer, UPST, VRNS, XMTR, Zalando, ZBRA. Post-market: ALAB, AMD, ANET, ANGI, BKNG, CPNG, DUOL, FLYW, FRSH, HURN, NVTS, OUST, PCOR, RVLV, SWKS, TOST, TREE, TRVG, XYZ.
